summary: Tsuzuki proves compatible and unique maximal-slope lifting on curves over perfect residue fields, and isomorphism of irreducible Q̄_p coefficients in higher dimension over finite fields; lifting a specified morphism in the latter setting retains the extra endomorphism condition. The extraction is partial: 165 located items and three ownership routes do not close the external proof, coefficient-descent, finite-étale and example obligations. Independent review corrects the signed-slope API, generic localization, locators, title and shared Chebotarev supplier, verifies the source findings and adds two missed findings. Nothing is claimed formalized.

items.name: General pointwise slope classification
items.statement: Finite-dimensional isocrystals over the completed maximal unramified coefficient field with algebraically closed residue field admit the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition into rational-slope blocks. items.name: Globalizing unit-root local lattices
items.statement: A unit-root generic φ–∇ module with a bounded-disc lattice at every interior closed point and an Eα† lattice at every boundary point comes from a unit-root overconvergent F-isocrystal, unique up to isomorphism. Katz correspondence and finite local monodromy supply the descent.

items.name: Globalizing subobjects by interior and boundary lattices
items.statement: For an overconvergent curve M†, a generic submodule Lη with compatible bounded-disc lattices inside M at interior points and dagger lattices at boundary points is induced by a unique overconvergent subobject L†⊂M†. For rank r use its determinant line and recover it as the kernel of wedge with that line.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem. The rank-one normalization and coefficient descent are separated as item 165/G10, because Lemma 3.32 requires unit-root.

items.name: Kummer-twisted Legendre PBQ example
items.statement: For p odd, C=P¹_Fp\{0,1,∞}, let L† be first relative rigid cohomology of the Legendre elliptic family y²=x(x−1)(x−z), and twist by the quadratic character from w²=z(z−1). For p≡1 mod 4 and the unit root π_p of y²=x³−x, the source constructs a nonsplit extension 0→L†(χ)→M†→1(π_p²)→0 with maximal generic slopes 1 and 0 and two PBQ steps. Its cohomological K3 calculation and existence proof remain G4 in this checkpoint; this is not a self-extension.

items.statement: On an affine smooth lift with a slope-filtered convergent realization, the image of the dagger section module in the top convergent quotient is a finite dagger module with integrable connection and horizontal Frobenius, hence an overconvergent quotient. items.name: Saturation under finite coefficient extension and Frobenius iteration

items.name: Canonical saturation quotient on a variety
items.statement: Every overconvergent F-isocrystal M† has a saturated quotient M^(sat,†) whose canonical maps to the maximal-slope quotient agree on every slope-filtered affine dense open. items.statement: For the smooth varieties and dense open immersions used here, overconvergent restriction is fully faithful, and a subobject of the restriction of a global overconvergent coefficient extends globally in the cited source scope. items.statement: The forgetful functor from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful in Kedlaya's smooth-variety setting. It is not asserted essentially surjective.

items.name: Curve quasi-saturation rank equality
items.statement: Let M≠0 be a pure convergent curve coefficient, N† overconvergent with slope-filtered N, and N→M surjective. If the induced map of overconvergent N† sections into convergent M sections is injective on one affine dense open, then λmax(N)=slope(M) and rank Top(N)=rank M.

items.name: Boundary kernel's maximal PBQ piece descends
items.statement: With H=ker(N→M), the local dagger kernel Hα† may be smaller after completion than Hα. The local quasi-saturation theorem identifies their maximal-slope quotient ranks; their maximal PBQ submodules then agree after completion. This supplies the boundary lattices needed to globalize the maximal PBQ subobject of H and contradict section injectivity.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Curve irreducibility criterion
items.statement: For a nonzero overconvergent curve coefficient whose convergent realization has a slope filtration, irreducibility is equivalent to PBQ, saturation and irreducibility of its top convergent quotient.

items.name: Extensions with smaller subobject slope
items.statement: For 0→L†→M†→N†→0 on a curve, with irreducible ends and s_L<s_N, M† is not saturated; the extension is nonsplit iff M† is PBQ. Use a dense slope-filtered open when necessary.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Equal-slope extensions
items.statement: With the same irreducible-end hypotheses and s_L=s_N, M† is PBQ and saturated, Top(M) is reducible, and the original extension is nonsplit iff the induced top-quotient extension is nonsplit.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Extensions with larger subobject slope
items.statement: If s_L>s_N, the two-step extension is the PBQ filtration and is nonsplit iff M† is saturated. If additionally rank M†=2, it splits by convergent splitting and global full faithfulness; do not extend this rank-two conclusion indiscriminately.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Global recovery of saturated graded PBQ pieces
items.statement: For slope-filtered convergent realizations M,N on a smooth connected curve, an isomorphism of convergent bounded quotients N/N^b→M/M^b determines a unique compatible isomorphism of the sums of saturated graded PBQ pieces of N† and M†, with equal PBQ lengths.

items.name: Strong maximal-slope lifting on curves
items.statement: For smooth connected C over perfect k, M†,N† over K with slope-filtered convergent realizations and h:Top(N)→Top(M), assume either irreducibility of both and h≠0, or both PBQ and saturated and h invertible. Then there is a unique isomorphism N†→M† inducing h.

items.name: Weaker maximal-quotient hypothesis suffices
items.statement: The curve lifting conclusion still holds if specified quotients Top(M),Top(N) are isoclinic and all slopes of their kernels at every point are strictly smaller. Shrink to a dense open with full slope filtrations and extend the resulting morphism by dense full faithfulness.

Restriction of scalars gives Tr_K(T)=Tr_{L/K}(Tr_L T)=Σ_{τ:L→Qpbar over K}τ(Tr_L T). Use splitting after Qpbar-extension, not L⊗K L as a product without normality.

items.name: Rigid Lefschetz trace formula over coefficient fields
items.statement: For connected separated finite-type pure-d X/Fq and every n>0, Σ_{β∈X(F_(q^n))}Tr_L(F_β^n)=Σ_{i=0}^{2d}(−1)^iTr_L(F^n|H_c^i(X/K,M†)), with the stated coefficient linearizations. Excision, the ordinary trace formula and nondegenerate field trace prove the coefficient extension.

items.name: Finiteness of rigid cohomology with Frobenius coefficients
items.statement: For a separated finite-type k-scheme and overconvergent F-isocrystal, H^i and H_c^i are finite dimensional in the source's coefficient range. This is a theorem, not part of the definition of the cohomology object.

items.name: Compact-support Poincaré duality
items.statement: For smooth pure-d X, the rigid pairing H^i(X,M∨)×H_c^(2d−i)(X,M)→K(−d) is perfect with Frobenius compatibility. In particular a q^d eigenvalue on top compact cohomology detects a Frobenius-fixed vector in H⁰ of the dual.

items.name: Compact-support weight bounds

items.name: Pure-Hom Chebotarev application
items.statement: Let X/Fq be smooth connected separated finite type and M†,N† irreducible Qpbar-coefficient objects with N†∨⊗M† ι-pure. If their linearized F-fibers are isomorphic at every closed point of a dense open, then M†≅N†. Equality of local factors, the weight-zero Hom pole and duality yield a nonzero global morphism. Import the generic coefficient Chebotarev theorem once from the common arithmetic-D-module continuation proposed by PAPER-ABE-18/51; mixedness/purity from item 140 permits this application to the present irreducibles. The source’s pure-Hom pole argument is an alternative proof, not a second generic Chebotarev programme.

items.statement: For irreducible overconvergent Qpbar coefficient M† on smooth connected X/Fq there is a dense open U such that every closed point of U lies on a smooth curve mapping to X whose pullback of M† is irreducible. AE supplies a stronger finite-set version; the one-point version suffices here.

routes.brief: Extend P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology) from its existing RD.0–RD.6 foundations, without rebuilding rings, frames, coefficient categories, local monodromy or rigid cohomology. The extension owns maximally bounded quotients, PBQ objects and filtrations, saturation, quasi-saturation and minimal/maximal-slope reconstruction. First derive local opposite-filtration rank equality with all coefficient-normalization and injectivity conditions. Construct generic bounded solutions and their base change, PBQ descent to bounded-disc and bounded Robba lattices, and globalization using the parent's interior/boundary gluing theorem. Use graded pieces P_i/P_(i−1), not nested P_i, in the decreasing slope and bounded-quotient formulas. Define saturation as a quotient by the kernel of the map to the maximal-slope quotient, and prove the v3 versions of 5.2 and 6.1. The curve target is Corollary 6.5: over a perfect residue field and the stated complete discrete valuation coefficient field, for slope-filtered realizations and h:Top(N)→Top(M), either irreducibility plus h≠0 or PBQ+saturation plus invertible h gives a UNIQUE overconvergent isomorphism inducing h. State the weaker quotient hypothesis of Remark 6.6 separately and dualize correctly to minimal subobjects. Develop LC with potentially different curves for the two coefficients; derive the two rank inequalities and closed-fiber identification. Import finite and Qpbar coefficient categories, coefficient projectors, trace, duality and real-weight conventions from RD.3–RD.6, and general Dieudonné–Manin point classification from Isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0). The higher-dimensional target is Theorem 7.20 over finite Fq with Qpbar coefficients: nonzero top-quotient h between irreducibles implies an isomorphism; inducing THAT h additionally needs, after finite constant extension, an irreducibility-preserving curve with bijective endomorphism restriction. Do not import later work to erase this distinction. Import the generic mixed coefficient Chebotarev theorem from the shared PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIArithmeticDModules proposal, specifically PAPER-ABE-18/51, and use the precisely sourced Abe–Esnault mixedness/purity input to obtain item 134. Tsuzuki’s pure-Hom pole proof is an alternative located proof at that common owner. The present continuation owns the minimal-slope application, finite-extension endomorphism lifting and projected trace average. PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20/109 in PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIRigidCompanions consumes the same generic supplier. Neither continuation should build a second generic Chebotarev or companion-existence theory. These proposed roadmap ids have no declaration-level stage yet; resolve that import in design without claiming an existing stage. The Legendre/Kummer K3 example, finite-étale PBQ proof, appendix Frobenius extension and all version/citation gaps must be resolved explicitly. Design at declaration granularity with APIs and at least three discriminating tests for every definition; this extraction does not authorize a Lean file.
